One embodiment provides an apparatus for analyzing body composition and hydration status by detecting the resistance of a human subject at zero and infinite frequency. The apparatus includes a method for indirectly measuring extracellular water mass, intracellular water mass, lean body mass, and body fat mass; daily changes in extracellular water mass, intracellular water mass, lean body mass, and body fat mass; acute changes in extracellular water mass and intracellular water mass; and individualized calibration of these indirect measurements.

In addition, the embodiment provides a method for fitting mathematical models to serial measurements of indirectly measured lean body mass and fat mass, as well as for dynamic, indirect, individualized measurement using minimum-variance estimation and prediction of daily changes in body composition, defined as changes in glycogen stores, fat stores, and protein stores; daily utilized macronutrient energy intake, defined as utilized carbohydrate, fat, and protein caloric intake; daily macronutrient oxidation rates, defined as rates of carbohydrate oxidation, fat oxidation, and protein oxidation; daily resting metabolic rate; daily unknown forms of energy losses or gains; daily rate of endogenous lipolysis; daily nitrogen excretion; daily gluconeogenesis from protein; daily determination of extracellular water mass; daily determination of intracellular water mass; and acute changes in extracellular water mass and intracellular water mass.

An apparatus embodiment is described for evaluating body composition and hydration by sensing a human subject’s electrical resistance at both zero frequency and infinite frequency. The apparatus includes a technique for indirectly determining extracellular water mass, intracellular water mass, lean body mass, and body fat mass; tracking day-to-day variations in extracellular water mass, intracellular water mass, lean body mass, and body fat mass; identifying short-term changes in extracellular and intracellular water mass; and providing subject-specific calibration for these indirect measurements.

The embodiment also includes a procedure for applying mathematical models to sequential measurements of indirectly assessed lean body mass and fat mass. It further enables dynamic, individualized indirect assessment through minimum-variance estimation and prediction of daily body-composition changes, including changes in glycogen stores, fat stores, and protein stores; daily utilized macronutrient energy intake, expressed as utilized carbohydrate, fat, and protein calories; daily macronutrient oxidation rates, including carbohydrate, fat, and protein oxidation rates; daily resting metabolic rate; daily unidentified energy gains or losses; daily endogenous lipolysis rate; daily nitrogen excretion; daily gluconeogenesis from protein; daily measurement of extracellular water mass; daily measurement of intracellular water mass; and acute changes in extracellular water mass and intracellular water mass.
outputs.L3:
The apparatus analyzes body composition and hydration status by measuring the electrical resistance of the human body at zero frequency and at infinite frequency. These resistance values provide information about how electrical current interacts with different body fluid compartments, allowing the system to evaluate the distribution of water inside and outside the body’s cells.

Using these measurements, the method indirectly determines key physiological parameters, including extracellular water mass, intracellular water mass, lean body mass, and body fat mass. Because these values are derived from electrical resistance rather than measured directly, the system applies mathematical relationships and calibration procedures to estimate body composition and hydration status.

The method is also designed to monitor both daily and acute changes in the body. It can track variations in body water, lean body mass, and body fat mass over time, making it useful for observing short-term hydration shifts as well as longer-term trends in body composition. This allows changes caused by diet, exercise, illness, fluid intake, or other physiological factors to be assessed more effectively.

The system supports individualized calibration to improve the accuracy of indirect body composition and hydration measurements. By adapting the measurement model to the characteristics of a specific individual, the apparatus can provide more personalized estimates than would be possible using generalized population-based assumptions alone.

In addition, the method uses mathematical modeling and minimum variance estimation techniques to evaluate daily metabolic changes. These models may be used to estimate energy intake, substrate oxidation rates, resting metabolic rate, and related physiological measures. By combining body composition data, hydration measurements, and metabolic modeling, the system provides a comprehensive framework for assessing changes in hydration, body composition, and metabolism over time.
outputs.L4:
The apparatus and methods described provide a system for assessing body composition, hydration status, and related physiological conditions by measuring the electrical properties of the human body. In particular, the system determines or estimates human electrical resistance at very low, effectively zero, frequency and at very high, effectively infinite, frequency. These measurements are used because different electrical frequencies interact differently with body tissues and fluids. Low-frequency current primarily reflects conductive pathways through extracellular fluid, while high-frequency current can pass more completely through both extracellular and intracellular compartments. By analyzing these resistance values, the system can indirectly estimate the distribution of water inside and outside the body’s cells.

The method may include taking one or more bioelectrical impedance or resistance measurements from a person using electrodes placed on selected body locations. The measured data may then be processed using individualized calibration information, such as the person’s height, weight, age, sex, body type, activity level, or previously measured physiological values. Rather than relying only on generalized population equations, the system can use personal calibration factors to improve accuracy for a specific individual. This allows the apparatus to generate estimates that are more closely matched to the user’s own physiology.

Using mathematical models, the system can convert the measured resistance values into estimates of extracellular water, intracellular water, and total body water. From these water compartments, the system can further derive or estimate lean body mass, fat mass, and changes in body composition over time. Because lean tissue contains a high proportion of water and fat tissue contains relatively little water, changes in measured resistance and modeled fluid volumes can be used to infer changes in muscle, fat, and overall body composition.

The system is also designed to analyze serial measurements, meaning that repeated measurements are collected over time and compared with one another. These measurements may be taken daily, multiple times per day, before and after exercise, during dietary changes, during illness or recovery, or in response to specific interventions such as hydration, fasting, training, or supplementation. By modeling trends rather than relying only on single measurements, the method can identify meaningful physiological changes and distinguish them from short-term measurement noise.

In addition to estimating body water and tissue composition, the apparatus and methods may be used to infer metabolic information. Changes in body mass, water distribution, resistance values, and composition estimates can be mathematically analyzed to estimate macronutrient use, including the relative oxidation of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins. The system may also estimate metabolic rate, energy expenditure, energy intake, and energy balance. For example, serial changes in body composition and hydration may be used to determine whether a person is in an energy deficit, energy surplus, or approximate energy balance.

The methods may further support acute monitoring of short-term physiological changes. These may include dehydration, rehydration, glycogen depletion or replenishment, fluid shifts between extracellular and intracellular compartments, changes associated with exercise, heat exposure, travel, illness, or changes in salt and carbohydrate intake. Because water balance and electrolyte distribution can change rapidly, repeated electrical resistance measurements can provide useful information about hydration and cellular fluid status.

The apparatus may include sensors, electrodes, a current source, measurement circuitry, a processor, memory, and software for applying calibration and modeling algorithms. It may be implemented as a dedicated body-composition device, a wearable or portable monitor, a scale-based system, a handheld device, or another electronic health-monitoring platform. The system may display results to the user, store historical measurements, transmit data to a remote device or cloud platform, and provide individualized feedback or recommendations.

Overall, the described technology enables indirect estimation and tracking of extracellular water, intracellular water, total body water, lean mass, fat mass, macronutrient utilization, substrate oxidation, metabolic rate, and energy balance. By combining electrical resistance measurements at limiting frequencies with individualized calibration and mathematical modeling of serial data, the system supports personalized monitoring of body composition, hydration, metabolism, and related physiological changes. It is suitable for both routine daily tracking and acute monitoring during periods of exercise, dietary modification, illness, recovery, or other changing physiological conditions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an apparatus and method that uses bioelectrical impedance at zero and infinite frequency to analyze human body composition, hydration status, extracellular/intracellular water, lean mass, fat mass, and metabolic changes over time.
counterfactuals.output: An apparatus and method are provided for assessing human body composition and physiological status using bioelectrical impedance measurements acquired over a plurality of frequencies and extrapolated to zero-frequency and infinite-frequency impedance values. The apparatus includes one or more electrode pairs configured to apply an electrical excitation signal to a body segment or whole body and to detect resulting voltage responses, a signal generation and measurement circuit, and a processor configured to determine resistance, reactance, phase angle, and impedance parameters representative of extracellular and intracellular conductive pathways. The processor derives a zero-frequency resistance associated primarily with extracellular water and an infinite-frequency resistance associated with total body water, and computes intracellular water, extracellular water, hydration status, lean body mass, fat mass, and related body-composition indices. In certain embodiments, the processor applies a dispersion model to multi-frequency impedance data to estimate limiting impedance values and to track temporal changes in fluid distribution, cellular integrity, nutritional status, and metabolic condition. The method includes obtaining impedance data from a subject, determining zero- and infinite-frequency impedance parameters, calculating body-water compartments and tissue composition, comparing results with stored subject-specific or population reference values, and generating output indicative of hydration, lean mass, fat mass, and metabolic changes over time.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.output: **Abstract** — A bioimpedance-based human health analysis device is disclosed for noninvasive assessment of body composition, hydration status, and metabolic characteristics. The device applies multi-frequency electrical excitation through body-contact electrodes and measures voltage and current responses to determine bioimpedance parameters, including resistance extrapolated at zero frequency and resistance extrapolated at infinite frequency. These resistance values are used to estimate extracellular and intracellular water compartments and total body water. The device dynamically processes impedance spectra, demographic inputs, anthropometric data, and temporal measurement trends to calculate fat mass, fat-free or lean mass, basal or resting metabolic rate, and indices of substrate oxidation, including relative carbohydrate and lipid utilization. In some embodiments, repeated or continuous measurements are analyzed to identify acute hydration changes, fluid shifts, edema, dehydration, or exercise- and nutrition-related alterations in body water distribution. The system may include signal-generation circuitry, sensing circuitry, a processor executing compartmental and predictive models, memory for storing longitudinal data, and a user interface or communication module for reporting health metrics. By integrating frequency-dependent resistance measurements with adaptive physiological modeling, the device provides real-time or near-real-time evaluation of body composition, metabolic state, and hydration dynamics for clinical, fitness, wellness, or remote-monitoring applications.
